fork.title: Attack two targets at once
fork.goal: Identify two targets, then find a move or short sequence that attacks both before your opponent can defend them.

questions.0pwjJ: Which targets could become vulnerable after the next exchange?
questions.0tMv4: What checks could change which pieces are available to attack?
questions.0bg6I: Which move could create a piece that threatens more than one target?
questions.0Jalw: What can you prepare now so a later threat attacks more than one target?
questions.00rw0: Which replies would you check before committing to a tactical sequence?
questions.0Ozbu: What can a series of checks do to the position of the targets?

sacrifice.title: Give up material for a concrete gain
sacrifice.goal: Calculate the opponent’s best reply before offering material and identify what you gain by the end of the line.

questions.0twue: What could change around the king if your opponent accepts a capture?
questions.0GrCZ: Which check could change the defender’s role after a recapture?
questions.07KFG: What would you look for after drawing a defender away?
questions.0YTZr: How would you tell whether an early offer pays off a few moves later?
questions.0sfEC: Which escape squares would you track as the king moves?
questions.0Hk7S: What would your opponent have to cover if the first offer is accepted?

pin.title: Use the piece that cannot move freely
pin.goal: Trace the line through a potentially pinned piece to the target behind it, then check which replies remain legal or worthwhile.

questions.0tEtC: Which exchanges could leave a defender tied to a more important target?
questions.0LmpF: What would a defender expose by leaving its line?
questions.0Svc3: Which replies could a piece still make while it is tied to the king?
questions.0iVzE: Which capture would you reconsider after tracing the defenders along the line?
questions.0RCJD: What changes if a defender has to choose between two duties?
questions.0oBJd: Which apparent defensive moves should you test before choosing a check?

kingsideAttack.title: Calculate an attack on the kingside
kingsideAttack.goal: Map the king’s exits and its defenders, then compare checks and captures by calculating the opponent’s strongest reply.

questions.0L6uG: Which nearby squares can the king use if it comes under attack?
questions.0Qp6f: What would you look for if a check draws a defender away?
questions.0mKLS: Which squares would the king still have after each check?
questions.0Ntdw: What other ways of giving check should you compare besides moving a major piece?
questions.0xqrT: How can you keep track of the king’s exits through a series of checks?
questions.00TJN: Which reply would you calculate first before continuing the attack?
